notes:
Rove 0.1.7 beta improves response reading, Regression lifecycle, Request transport and update/close reliability.

- PDF and HTML responses use one contextual toolbar below response tabs. Secondary actions are grouped in More, search opens on demand, and document zoom supports keyboard and platform gestures. PDF rendering recovers after pane resize/reveal. HTML images, styles and fonts load automatically, with unavailable-asset details in More.
- Regression Suites support Setup → Cases → Teardown, shared Run values and bounded cleanup after ordinary cancellation. Desktop and CLI reports preserve lifecycle phases. Script Helper keeps contextual documentation beside functions.
- Request timeout and redirect preferences can inherit Network settings or be overridden per Request. Supported Bruno/Postman settings import into one reviewed transport setup flow.
- Closing a Request offers Cancel, Close, or Save and Close. Ordinary clean authoring no longer requires a successful recovery cache write before update/quit; unsaved work and active or uncertain writes keep their guards. Recovery confirmation, retry and editor reload checks preserve current work.
- The request-name field uses less vertical space while retaining its accessible name.
- History copy/export masks credential query parameters consistently, including the first parameter of an absolute URL. Source Control rejects Windows drive paths consistently across platforms.

Compatibility: saved Requests with transport overrides use Request schema v24; Suites with lifecycle sections use Suite schema v2. Older clients reject unsupported new definitions rather than silently changing their execution.

The beta remains an optional update with minimum supported version 0.1.1. An older client already blocked by its running recovery/update gate may still need the manual installer once; downloading this release cannot replace code before installation. Installed upgrade/data preservation and native gesture behavior require platform acceptance. macOS packages use ad-hoc platform signing and are not Apple-notarized.
